layout: app/modules/legal_share/ — service.py (CASE_SHARE + REVIEW_THREAD overlay stores), router.py (APIRouter at /api/legal-share + pages_router at root for /legal-share and /r/{token}), register.py (5 function groups), module_contract.json, tests/. Tenant page: /legal-share renders pages/legal_share.html. Reviewer page: /r/{token} renders pages/reviewer_share.html (or reviewer_unavailable.html for expired/revoked/unknown tokens).

input_audit.note: Incident id — resolved against the tenant's own INCIDENT overlays via case_review.service.resolve_case; 404 if not theirs.
Tenant-chosen display name for the reviewer (e.g. 'Attorney Lee'). Not an identity — display only.
Vault document ids the reviewer may read. Enforced at every reviewer read; documents are verified against the owner's vault at share creation.
Enum: 7 | 30 | 90. Share expiry in days from creation.
Tenant-side share management identifier (CASE_SHARE payload share_id).
Owner-scoped share token '{user_id}:{urlsafe32}' — the entire reviewer credential. Resolves the owner vault with no server-side index.
Vault document id a reviewer question attaches to; must be inside the share's document scope.
Vault document id for metadata/content reads; enforced against share scope.
REVIEW_THREAD payload thread_id (or overlay_id); lookup verifies the owning case anchor.
Question/answer text — stored verbatim; Semptify never drafts or suggests legal content.
yellow_access cookie/session for tenant routes. Reviewer routes take no user_id — the token is the credential.

preview_state: Reviewer sees the shared slice only: case summary, selected documents (metadata + read-only byte stream), evidence notes, deadlines, and this share's threads. Expired/revoked/unknown tokens render a calm 'not available' page.
review_state: Tenant sees every share with access count, last opened, unread question count, and full threads; revoke is a deliberate bottom-of-page action.
output_how: CASE_SHARE overlays anchored 'case-shares:{effective_id}' at VAULT_RECORDS_FILE; REVIEW_THREAD overlays anchored 'review-threads:{case_id}' at VAULT_CASE_REVIEW_FILE — both written via UnifiedOverlayManager into the tenant's own OAuth-connected cloud vault.
output_where: Tenant's cloud vault — Semptify servers hold no share state and no thread content.
output_why: Lets a tenant hand a structured case file to an outside attorney/advocate with document-tied Q&A, without the reviewer needing any Semptify identity.
process_description: Tenant picks a case → picks which documents/notes/deadlines are shared (filed material on by default, drafts off) → names the reviewer → picks expiry (7/30/90 days) → gets a /r/{token} link. The reviewer opens the link anonymously, reads documents, and asks questions tied to specific documents. The tenant sees unread questions and replies in their own words. Revoke or expiry closes the share. Creating a share sets legal_share_initialized through the existing Case Review path.
process_context: Supersedes Case Review spec §8 (sharing outside Semptify) — Brad approved in-Semptify sharing 2026-09-27. Replaces the OneDrive folder-tree + index-file workflow with the same structure plus a per-document question action.

narrative_events.context_clause: because the tenant chose to share selected case material with a reviewer

narrative_events.object: a reviewer question on a shared document
narrative_events.context_clause: while the reviewer was reading the shared case file

invariants: The reviewer has no Semptify identity — no account, no role, no login; the owner-scoped token is the entire credential.
No write/edit path to original documents exists anywhere in this module — reviewer reads stream through shared_document_stream only.
certified is hardcoded False on every overlay this module creates.
Share grants, threads, questions, and answers persist only as overlays in the tenant's vault — no server-side case-content tables.
Reviewer scope is the share's explicit document id list; out-of-scope ids return document_not_shared.
Revocation and expiry are enforced at the token gate on every reviewer request, not just at page load.
All thread text is authored by the party who typed it — no Semptify-generated legal content.
